Asciinema's 3.0 player rebuild used SolidJS, and the commenter cites the result as 4x smaller and 50x faster.
The performance SolidJS gets out of the DOM is "next level" and the project is very approachable. However, the docs could use a section on migrating from React to SolidJS.

User worries about the docs' warning that destructuring or early property access on props/stores can lose reactivity. Asks whether SolidJS offers a lint or warning for this, noting TypeScript doesn't catch it.

Ported react-bootstrap to SolidJS and found it fairly painless. Components running only once means no need to stash useRefs/useCallbacks, and refs are just the elements. Porting was mostly removing awkward React code plus a few Solid functions to keep split props reactive. "A+ for Solid developer experience" after 5+ years of React.
Coming from Vue, the user found Solid such a pleasant library to use, intuitive in the way Vue was.
The playground widget on the SolidJS landing page misbehaved: dragging the slider to enlarge the code section showed only a sliver of about 2 lines. "Doesn't make a very good first impression."
On Android Chrome, some examples on the Solid site (CSS animations, todo) didn't load or contained errors.

Uses Solid as a go-to for data viz because it is small and easy to inject into other pages. Favourite feature is opt-in reactivity: instead of wasted re-renders and useMemo as in React, you declare granular computed properties and Solid handles updates. Rough edges: the special props object and boilerplate function calls.
Critic finds the SolidJS API non-intuitive and its reactive system worse than Svelte's. They see hook-like concepts as no progress and say Svelte reactivity is something you don't think about.

Having used Solid on a largish web product for over a year, the user will not return to React. They value that everything in the reactive system is immediate, which keeps state changes intuitive and easy to debug.
Hesitant to learn Solid in detail because an upcoming 2.0 may bring many breaking changes.
Big fan of Solid, but notes it's not widely used, with little marketing or real app/product/DX focus from the project.

Loves that Solid has feature parity with React and is faster. Its small commit history (about 1,823 commits, mostly the creator's) gives confidence for long-term maintenance, compared with a bloated, frequently pivoting React.

Writing Solid after a workday of React feels liberating, and it is expressive with solid-primitives. Ecosystem gaps are real, though. The tRPC v10 adapter is unmaintained, and v11 lacks tanstack-query integration. Framer motion lags versions behind React.

Uses React at work and Solid for side projects. After an office presentation, a colleague said it looks like React but is easier to understand, faster, smaller, with more built in, and asked why they weren't using it.
Annoyance coming from React: props must be passed as functions returning values rather than plain values, otherwise the prop can never update.

Loves Solid's simple state handling (no keys, deep state, no reducer) but finds it unpolished. Specific complaints: questions go unanswered, docs are lacking, and dev tools are alpha/unusable. Suspense should be avoided, createUniqueId isn't very unique, and SolidStart routing is occasionally very slow with no workaround. Good for small experienced teams.
Svelte is far superior: you write plain HTML instead of Solid's verbose JSX syntax.
Solid realizes the full potential of fine-grained reactive updates, a concept from Knockout, Qt, Aurelia and MobX. "Definitely worth checking out."
"This is the single best JavaScript framework for frontend development at the moment."
